summary: 504s and large latency spikes for generations with very large max_tokens / extended contexts
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using very large max_tokens and long prompt contexts are receiving 504 gateway timeouts and large tail latencies for generation requests. Errors started increasing after the runtime release 2026.03.08 which included a kernel-selection optimization and new KV cache eviction heuristics.

Impact:
- NovaSearch (enterprise) reports ~12% of their long-run generation attempts (max_tokens >= 100k) are returning 504s in us-east.
- A few other self-serve and dedicated customers have sporadic timeouts when using streaming + extended contexts.
- User-facing impact: end-users see truncated responses or failed generations for long-document summarization and ingestion jobs.

Environment:
- prod: us-east cluster serving mixed hosted/dedicated workloads
- Affected models: gptx-32k-quant, gptx-64k-legacy pinned on customer accounts
- API: /v1/generate streaming and non-streaming endpoints

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) POST /v1/generate with model=gptx-32k-quant, prompt size ~80k tokens, max_tokens=120000, stream=true
2) Observe streaming chunks for first ~30s then connection reset and final 504 from API gateway
3) Repeat without streaming: request eventually returns 504 at ~90s

Observed behavior / logs:
- API gateway returns HTTP 504 with backend timeout in access logs.
- Serving runtime traces show sudden CPU/GPU stalls where token emit rate drops to near-zero for long sequences, followed by a burst when resumed.
- Datadog traces: per-token generation latency increases linearly after token index ~50k.
- There are correlated kernel-selection WARN logs that show fallback to a slower execution path on long sequences.

Initial hypothesis:
- Kernel-selection heuristic is choosing a slow fallback path for very long sequence lengths (after regression in 2026.03.08).
- KV cache eviction / re-materialization is causing recompute of attention and major compute overhead for long contexts.
- API gateway default backend timeout (90s) is not sufficient for extreme max_tokens workloads that naturally take minutes.

Temporary mitigations attempted:
- Support suggested customer reduce max_tokens and/or chunk prompts and stream partial results.
- Routed NovaSearch traffic to a dedicated capacity pool (higher priority), which reduced 504s but did not eliminate the per-token slowdown.
- Rolled back a small runtime tuning (2026.03.10) for a customer test; saw partial improvement.

Next steps:
- SRE to reproduce on internal staging with a 100k-token synthetic prompt (assigned to Diego).
- Runtime engineering to review kernel-selection code path and KV cache heuristics (PR referenced).
- Short-term: propose increasing API gateway backend timeout for enterprise customers running long generations, plus a customer-facing docs note explaining limits and recommended patterns.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 Diego: Spun up a prod-like staging cluster and replayed the customer workload. Observed per-token latency ramp after ~48k tokens. GPU utilization remained stable; CPU pre/post-processing spikes correlated with recompute events.

2026-03-12 Marcus (Runtime Eng): Found a change in PR #2689 that altered kernel selection thresholds for sequence chunking; on long sequences it triggers a 'safe' but slower kernel (observed orders-of-magnitude slower for >50k tokens).
2026-03-13 Support (Lena): Confirmed NovaSearch can accept routing to dedicated pool and temporary increase of gateway timeout; still sees occasional multi-minute stalls on streaming.

2026-03-13 Diego: Captured detailed traces (Datadog trace IDs: trace.prod.us-east.20260313.7a8c) and uploaded serving runtime debug dump to S3: s3://redwood-debug/long-context/SUP-6489/dump-20260313.tar.gz

2026-03-14 Marcus: Created fix branch that restores prior kernel threshold behavior and adds a targeted optimization for KV cache spans. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2741
2026-03-14 Diego: Coordinating a canary rollout of the fix to a small subset of dedicated capacity tomorrow morning (2026-03-15).
comments: Lena Park (2026-03-12): Customer reported spike after last runtime release. They provided example request payload and request IDs; attaching here for trace: req-20260312-nova-83f.
Diego Rivera (2026-03-12): Reproducing on staging; collecting GPU/CPU traces. Assigned to runtime eng for kernel-selection review.
Marcus Chen (Runtime Eng) (2026-03-13): Found related change in PR #2689. Working on a revert/patch. Initial microbenchmarks show a 4-6x improvement on long-context paths after patch.

Lena Park (2026-03-13): Shared mitigation guidance with NovaSearch: 1) reduce max_tokens where possible, 2) enable chunked streaming, 3) request temporary routing to dedicated pool. Customer agreed to canary traffic test.
Diego Rivera (2026-03-14): Will coordinate canary rollout with infra at 2026-03-15 09:00 UTC. Scheduling post-canaried perf validation and rollback plan.
NovaSearch (Customer) (2026-03-14): Appreciates quick response; requests ETA for permanent fix and asks whether contract credits are possible for impacted runs.
resolution: Workarounds applied: 1) Routed NovaSearch to dedicated pool and temporarily increased backend timeout for their tenant to 300s. 2) Customer instructed on chunking/streaming patterns. Root cause: regression in kernel-selection thresholds that selected a slower execution path for sequences > ~50k tokens leading to KV re-materialization and per-token recompute. Fix implemented in PR #2741; canary rollout scheduled 2026-03-15. Post-rollout validation required. Follow-up: update runtime unit tests to cover long-sequence kernel selection and add a customer-facing note to docs about practical max_tokens guidance.
